# Log

Gives the logarithm of a number, natural or to a given base.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
Log(value, [base])
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | The number, above zero. Zero or a negative number is a runtime error, and so is null or a value that is not a number. |
| `base` | number, optional | The base of the logarithm, above zero and not 1; zero, a negative number or 1 is a runtime error, and so is a value that is not a number. When it is left out, or null, the natural logarithm, to base e, is given. |

## Returns

Number. The logarithm of value to base. When value and base are both exact and value is base raised to an integer power, that integer is returned exactly; otherwise the result is rounded to the nearest floating-point value. Never null.

## Example

`Log(1000, 10)` returns `3`.

`Log(1)` returns `0`.
